newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen bank 96 pre-tax profit up at 350 mln yuan.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen bank 96 pre-tax profit up at 350 mln yuan.

text.p: The Shenzhen City United Bank, a joint-stock commercial bank founded in June 1995, posted pre-tax profits of 350 million yuan for 1996, state media said on Thursday.

The bank, whose assets totalled 16.8 billion yuan at end-1996 compared with 13.3 billion yuan at the beginning of 1996, had exceeded its 1996 pre-tax profit target by 52.7 percent, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said.

The bank's outstanding deposits reached 9.1 billion yuan as of the end of 1996, up by 31.9 percent compared with 6.9 billion yuan at the beginning of last year, with outstanding loans hitting 6.0 billion yuan, up 16.7 percent from 5.14 billion yuan at the beginning of the year, the newspaper said.
The steady growth was fuelled by the bank's moves to attract deposits and improve the structure of its loans, a bank official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

The bank, formed through the merger of 165 small city credit co-operatives, has 17 branches operating more than 30 deposit offices across the 300 sq-km Shenzhen Special Economic Zone, the official said.
More than 60 percent of the bank's loans went to city government infrastructure projects, including the construction of Yantian Harbour, Shenzhen Airport and some highways, he said.
Most of the remaining 30 percent of loans went to small and medium-sized industrial enterprises, he said.

The bank's non-performing loan ratio was rather low, he said but did not give a figure. The bank has a total share capital of one billion shares, 25 percent of which is held by the Shenzhen municipal government and the rest by a number of institutions, the official said.
